question.text: A Delhi-based portfolio manager wants to replicate a NIFTY 500 index portfolio for a client with an AUM of Rs. 12 crore. Several smallcap constituents trade thinly. Which indexing technique is most appropriate?

answer.text: Sampling — pick liquid, similar-risk proxies for illiquid constituents
Buy and hold on top 50 stocks only
Only invest via an index future on NIFTY 500

explanation.text: The Logic: Sampling addresses the two problems of full replication on a large/illiquid index: illiquid constituents and high transaction cost. The manager picks liquid stocks with similar sector/market-cap/risk profile to mimic index mean-variance. The Trap: Full replication of NIFTY 500 at Rs.12 cr will bleed on impact cost; top-50 only abandons the mandate; futures on NIFTY 500 don't exist as retail derivative. Cross-Exam Context: XV covers similar concepts for research; XIX-A/B use it for allocation. XXI-B expects you to choose technique based on AUM and liquidity. Manager's Pro-Tip: Below the threshold AUM, sampling often beats full replication on cost even if tracking error is marginally higher.
